Author: Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari

1  IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE  CRA No. 7336 of 2023  (SHIVA Vs THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH)
 Dated : 15-05-2024  Shri Akhilesh Kumar Saxena - Advocate for the appellant  Shri G S Chouhan - Government Advocate for the responde Heard o n I.A. No. 8404/2023, which is the first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed under section 389 (1)of the Cr.P.C. on behalf of sole appellant - Shiva S/o Shri Premnarayan.
Appellant has been convicted in Special Case No. 70/2019 by 13th Additional Sessions Judge and Special Judge POCSO Act, District Indore vide judgment dated 17.05.2023 under Section 363 of IPC, 366 of IPC, 376(1), 376 (3) of IPC and Section 4 read with Section 3 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo 7 years RI, 10 years R.I and 20 years RI to be run concurrently and fine with default stipulations for committing penetrative sexual assault towards victim (PW-2) aged 15 years,
6 months on 01.03.2019 after kidnapping the child from the custody of her guardians.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This application has been preferred on the ground that the trial Court has committed error by ignoring the contradictions between the statement of victim (Exhibit-D-1).
Doctor Vibhuthi Thakur (PW-4) has not found any mark of injury on the body of the victim and there is no finding regarding the penetrative sexual assault towards the victim.
FSL report (Exhibit-P-8) does not mention the findings regarding the penetrative sexual assault towards the victim.
The appellant is the only earning member of the family and residence of District Khargone.
The findings of conviction and sentence is not based on proper appreciation of the evidence.
Despite service of summons no one appeared on behalf of victim.

Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future, therefore, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.

On the other hand learned Govt. Advocate has opposed the prayer by submitting the reply through Document No. 11687 of 2023 wherein it is stated that the conviction is based on proper appreciation of evidence and appellant accused has failed to discharge the onus of rebutting the presumption under Section 29 of the POCSO Act, 2012 by leading evidence, therefore, no case for grant of suspension is made out.

sentences.text: We have heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.

In light of the date of birth of the victim (PW-2) on the date of incident i.e on 01.03.2019 the victim was 15 years and six months and recovery of the victim after three days on 04.03.2019 vide Exhibit-P-3 and in the light of the statement of the victim (PW-2), we are not inclined to suspend the jail sentence of the appellant accused at present.
List this matter for final hearing in due course.
